column1: # 25장 말투 지시(11-10). 열: 조각 앞머리 → 지시(영어, 짧게). @scene 행은 장면 설명. 엄마 편지(@letter 윤하야.)는 지시하지 않는다.

column2: The envelope from Korea with her mother's birth certificate has sat unopened for a week; she is afraid the dates will prove something that would keep her from Marc. Vale, the young Argentine lodger, teases her: is she going to open it or hatch it like a hen ("empollar")? At night Montse, the landlady, proposes opening it on Saturday at the Castanyada, with everyone, and says Marc will bring his grandfather's notebook from 1974. Tense underneath, softened by kindness and humor.
anxious, holding still

column1: ¿Lo vas a abrir o lo vas a empollar?
column2: teasing, Rioplatense; "empollar" means sitting on eggs, "Como una gallina" explains the joke
small and honest
gentle under the teasing
calm and kind; "la noche de las castañas" explains the name of the festival
curious, a little wary
plain, letting it land; "La de 1974" quietly

column1: Nena, lo malo, mejor con castañas.
column2: wry comfort, sitting down beside her

October 31, the Castanyada, the old Catalan chestnut festival. Montse explains its origin while she, Vale and Yuna make panellets (almond sweets) in the kitchen; Vale keeps eating them. At six Yuna buys chestnuts and sweet potatoes from a chestnut seller under the clock tower in Gràcia. Warm, homely, a calm before the envelope.
warm, explaining

column1: Antes, en la noche de Todos los Santos
column2: telling an old custom while working with her hands, warm
scolding her for eating the sweets, fond
cheeky excuse, Rioplatense; "Control de calidad" deadpan

column1: 여섯 시에 몬세가 돈을 쥐여 주며
column2: happy, autumn evening
careful, a learner ordering correctly
warm street seller's call, with a wink

Eight o'clock, Montse's kitchen table: Montse, Vale, Yuna and Marc, the reserved locksmith, who is still awkward with Yuna after their quarrel. They eat chestnuts and panellets; nobody mentions the envelope. Then Yuna opens it: a 1975 birth certificate from Las Palmas and a 1974 watch-repair receipt signed "M. Puig". Marc recognises his grandfather Martí's handwriting. Suspense, quiet.
quiet, a little tense

column1: A la mesa. Las castañas frías
column2: brisk and warm, rescuing an awkward moment
quietly, pushing the plate away: time to open the envelope
slow and tense, reading official papers
quiet, stunned recognition

column1: @scene 마르크가 검은 수첩의 첫 장을 열었다
column2: Same table. Marc reads aloud from his grandfather Martí's 1974 notebook: Martí arrived in Las Palmas only in September, too late to be the father of Yuna's mother, born February 1975. A later entry mentions a Korean sailor, Yuna's grandfather, whose wife was expecting a baby. Montse explains that this sailor later brought Yuna's grandmother to her house. Relief and wonder; Montse and Yuna both say "ojalá…" (if only) about what they should have said or asked.

column1: 마르크가 검은 수첩의 첫 장을 열었다
column2: hushed, listening closely
reading his grandfather's notebook aloud, steady and careful
counting, then slowly relieved
reading on, voice lower, aware of what it means
slowly realizing, relief rising; repeating the line from the notebook
telling the story at last, warm; "No por casualidad. Por un reloj." very soft
gently, not blaming

column1: Sabía que el marinero era un cliente
column2: regretful, honest; "Ojalá te lo hubiera dicho" soft, full of regret

column1: No. Ojalá yo te lo hubiera preguntado
column2: gently taking the blame herself
laughing with wet eyes, affectionate

Yuna reads her mother's letter from Korea, then translates part of it aloud into Spanish for the others, her first translation. Her mother thanks the man from the clock shop who took her to hospital as a baby and stayed all night. Montse remembers that night on the bench at Sant Pau. Moved, gentle.
quiet, private
careful, moved
translating aloud for the first time, careful and slow, moved
remembering, hand on her heart, tender; "Era vuestra" gentle and clear

Later, on the same rooftop where Marc and Yuna argued. Yuna apologizes again; Marc, a man of few words, answers with "si yo fuera tú" (if I were you) and finally smiles. They make up and agree to meet at the workshop on Tuesday. Quiet warmth after a long tension.
calm, a different quiet
a sincere apology, steady

column1: Ya me lo dijiste en el Palau.
column2: dry, not unkind
gentle and sure
honest, measured; a little softer at the end
quietly admitting it
dry, then a smile in his voice
warm, an invitation; "El reloj te espera" softly
lightly amused, content
